subject.title: File Browser: Remove ALLOWED_FILE_NAMES whitelist, add scope levels

question: Should OpenClaw expose workspace-wide and/or host-system file browsing from Control UI and Gateway, and under what operator scopes and safety limits?
rationale: The workspace scope broadens Gateway file access and the system scope crosses the agent workspace boundary, so code inspection cannot choose the product/security boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve Workspace Only
options.body: Keep the current bootstrap-file API, pursue a bounded `agents.workspace.*` API for agent workspaces, and leave host-system browsing out of scope for now.

options.title: Approve Workspace And System Scopes
options.body: Allow both scopes only after maintainers define stronger auth, read/write defaults, path boundaries, audit behavior, limits, and destructive-operation UX.

options.title: Keep Current Core Surface
options.body: Reject the core expansion for now and direct users to terminal/plugin workflows such as `openclaw path` until a narrower product need is approved.

recommendation.title: Approve Workspace Only
recommendation.body: Keep the current bootstrap-file API, pursue a bounded `agents.workspace.*` API for agent workspaces, and leave host-system browsing out of scope for now.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history ties this person to the Gateway/protocol surfaces and the current allowlisted file helper that would need product/security boundary changes.
